newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares fall on inflation worries.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares fall on inflation worries.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial index tumbled 4.5 percent during the week ended Friday as investors' attention was diverted to the money market where interest rates have gained more than five percentage points in the last two weeks.
Worries that inflation is on the way up again have pushed interest rates above the 22 percent mark in the money market sparking jitters the era of high interest rates has returned.
The fears spread to the traditionally stabler mining index, sinking it 1.6 percent or 16.01 points during the week to close at 1002.53.
"But I think the market has bottomed out as volumes are increasing which means institutional investors are seeing value in shares again," one market analyst said.
He said more than 30 percent of the market, including blue chips Delta and Meikles, is expected to report in the next four weeks, providing the market with fresh news.
"The results should be good and the forecasts positive and that should underpin the market. I see the industrial index resuming its upward trend soon," the analyst added.
On Friday the index lost 40.27 or 0.39 percent to close at 10,303.24, on the back of losses in sugar producers ZSR down 125 cents to 1,300 and Hippo which dropped 35 to 1,575.
Retailers Edgars and cement manufacturers Porthold each shed 50 cents to 750 and 1, 650 respectively.
The mining index rose 0.55 percent or 5.46 points on Friday lifted by Wankie, which added 15 cents to 515 while Falgold was unchanged.
